title: Beyond the Trees Avondale: Treetop Walk & Tower
summary: 1.4km treetop walk, 38m viewing tower with slide, house tours, and café in Rathdrum.
description: Beyond the Trees Avondale reopened in June 2022 following a €19 million redevelopment project by Coillte in partnership with Fáilte Ireland and EAK Ireland. Located in Rathdrum, the site features the longest Treetop Walk in Ireland and the UK, stretching 1.4km. This journey through and above the trees culminates at the impressive Viewing Tower, which stands 38m above the forest. From here, visitors reveal panoramic 360-degree views over the Wicklow Mountains, the Avonmore River, and the Vale of Avoca. Both adults and children can opt to whizz back down the tower via the gigantic 90m spiral slide. The venue also offers a complimentary self-guided visit to the Coillte Pavilion, where visitors learn about the evolution of forestry in Ireland. Adjacent to the outdoor dining terrace of the Seed Café is an adventurous children's playground within the picturesque Walled Garden. The café crafts creative food offerings using high quality, local Wicklow ingredients. Guided tours of the historic 18th century Avondale House, titled 'At Home with the Parnells', are available to book in advance from Autumn 2022. These tours encompass the life and times of Charles Stewart Parnell, his mother Delia, and his sisters Fanny and Anna, who were co-founders of the Ladies Land League in 1881. From the Walled Gardens, there is access to the Treetop Walk, a stimulating sensory garden, and forest walking trails.

description: Beyond The Trees Avondale is located in Avondale Forest Park, Rathdrum, Co. Wicklow. The venue features a unique 1.3km treetop walk that allows visitors to journey through the forest and high above the canopy. The experience culminates at a 38m high Viewing Tower offering panoramic 360-degree views of the Wicklow Mountains, the Vale of Avoca, and the Avonmore River. Visitors can return to the ground via an optional gigantic 90m spiral slide. At Home with the Parnells offers guided tours of the historic 18th Century Avondale House. These 45-minute tours take place in multiple slots every day and cover the Parnell family heritage, including Charles Stewart Parnell and the forestry school history. The venue also features Ireland's first outdoor wooden marble run, which spans 50 metres and consists of eight interconnected wooden tables designed for hands-on physics learning. A contemporary Seed Café serves locally sourced food with views of the Walled Garden. The site includes an adventurous children's playground, a sensory garden, and forest walking trails. The Treetop Walk, Viewing Tower, and Avondale House are buggy and wheelchair accessible. U18s must be accompanied by an adult, and U6s require adult supervision on the slide.

title: Michael Collins House Museum, Clonakilty
summary: Museum in Clonakilty dedicated to Michael Collins, opened in 2016, with guided tours and interactive displays.
description: Michael Collins House Museum is located at 7 Emmet Square, Clonakilty, County Cork, Ireland. It is situated in a house built in the 1800s, restored to its original era layout on a Georgian square outside Dublin. The museum, which opened in 2016, is dedicated to Michael Collins, offering insight into his life as a farmer's son, rebel, politician, and soldier, known as 'The Big Fella'. It also explores local patriots like Jeremiah O'Donovan Rossa and the history of Irish independence, including the 1798 Rebellion. The venue features interactive displays, activity sheets, audio-visual presentations, artefacts, and information boards. It is suitable for all ages and levels of interest, promoting a family-friendly atmosphere. Popular with schools and tour groups, it offers curriculum-appropriate tours, age-appropriate worksheets, and bespoke options. Guided tours last approximately one hour for groups or 1.5 hours for school groups. The museum is fully wheelchair accessible and includes baby changing facilities, toilets, and a book and gift shop. Nearby picnic areas and parks are available, with free on-street parking. Coffee, lunch, and dinner offers are available in conjunction with the Emmet Hotel. The museum is open Tuesday to Saturday from 10am to 5pm, with last admission at 4pm.

title: Glendeer Pet Farm, Athlone
summary: Irish tourist board approved pet farm in Athlone with animals, play areas, and seasonal opening times.
description: Glendeer Pet Farm is an Irish tourist board approved pet farm located in Athlone, the heart of Ireland. Since opening its gates to the public in April 1991, the farm has been featured on numerous TV programmes and won several awards. Visitors can enjoy interactive animal experiences where they can feed, pet, and hold animals including guinea pigs, chicks, lizards, tortoises, deer, pigs, llamas, alpacas, emus, goats, donkeys, and sheep. The farm also offers cute cuddle baby animals such as kid goats, lambs, and rabbits. There is something for all ages, including a double obstacle course, a maze, a zipwire, a soft play toddler area, and a sand barn with diggers. An 1850s restored cottage and a secluded Fairy Trail are also available. The venue is suitable for any weather with indoor play areas and a large section of animals housed undercover. Facilities include a coffee shop, indoor and outdoor picnic areas, a children's playground, pets corner, toilets, baby changing facilities, a souvenir shop, and ample parking. The farm is wheelchair accessible and caters to groups with additional needs. Opening times run from March 16th to the end of September, closed on Tuesdays and Wednesdays in March, April, and May (excluding Easter Mid Term). Regular hours are Monday to Saturday from 11am to 6pm, and Sunday from 12pm to 6pm.

description: The Battle of the Boyne Visitor Centre is part of the Oldbridge Estate in Oldbridge, County Meath. The grounds allow dogs on leads but prohibit cycling, fire lighting, camping, and barbecues. There are wheelchair accessible facilities and toilets. The nearest train station is Thurles. During winter, the centre may close due to weather, and a hazard warning notes deep water nearby and uneven terrain.

title: Farmleigh House and Gardens: Edwardian Mansion
summary: Free grounds, gardens and gallery in Phoenix Park; paid house tours available.
description: Farmleigh is a 78-acre estate located inside Dublin's Phoenix Park. It is described as an eclectic Edwardian mansion and serves as the Irish state guesthouse. The property was constructed by Edward Cecil Guinness, great-grandson of Arthur Guinness, around a smaller Georgian house in the 1880s. The government purchased the estate in June 1999 to provide accommodation for high-level meetings and visiting guests. The site features a library with a collection of rare books and manuscripts, as well as extensive pleasure-grounds containing Victorian and Edwardian ornamental features, walled and sunken gardens, and scenic lakeside walks. The estate also includes a working farm with a herd of Kerry cows. Admission to the grounds, gardens, and gallery is free. title: University College Cork: 180th Anniversary Events

description: University College Cork is currently celebrating 180 years of excellence with a range of family-friendly activities, performances, exhibitions, and tours across its campus. The institution was established in 1845 and opened its gates to just 115 students in 1849. Today, it has a student population of over 26,000. UCC is ranked 220 in the prestigious QS World University Ranking and is also recognized as a world leader for societal impact. The university holds a unique distinction in Ireland as the only one awarded Sunday Times University of the Year on five occasions since the award's inception in 2002. Over 90% of its graduates enter employment or further studies. The university supports a global network of 225,000+ alumni. It is noted as the world's first 'Green Campus' and has a significant economic footprint, generating €3.2 million for the Irish economy every day, with a total economic impact of €1.18 billion annually. Additionally, 24% of student intake is through alternative access pathways. Visitors can explore the campus, which features the UCC Library and the Glucksman art gallery, where exhibitions such as The Annals of Inisfallen are displayed.

title: Shandon Tower, Bells & St. Anne's Church
summary: Historic church in Cork City with tower views and playable bells.
description: St. Anne's Church, Shandon Tower & Bells is located at Church Street, Shandon, Cork City, T23 YN88. St. Anne's is the oldest church still in continuous use in Cork City with weekly church services and an active worshipping congregation since 1722. The church and tower offer an interesting and memorable experience for young and old alike. Visitors can play the famous Shandon Bells, see the inner workings of the four-faced liar clock, and climb the tower to see the 360-degree views of Cork. Because visitors have to pass the bells at the top of the tower, ear defenders are provided at the entrance. The historic church is a member of the Church of Ireland and belongs to the worldwide Anglican (Episcopal) Communion. It is described as one of the most important early 18th-century churches in Ireland. The venue hosts a Christmas Market in 2026, specifically the Giving Thanks Christmas Market on 20–21 November 2026. The church also hosts special events to mark significant occasions in the Christian calendar, such as Christmas, Easter, Pentecost and Harvest Festival. Current opening hours are Monday to Saturday from 10:00 to 16:30, with last entry at 16:00. Sunday opening hours are from 12:00 to 16:30. A Sunday worship service is held at 10:15 am. The telephone number for the venue is +353 214505906.

title: Muckross House, Gardens and Traditional Farms
summary: Victorian mansion, gardens, and 1930s working farms in Killarney National Park.
description:
Muckross House, Gardens and Traditional Farms are located in The National Park, Killarney, Co Kerry, just 6km from the town centre. The present-day Muckross House was completed in 1843 and preserved as a late 19th-century mansion with original furnishings and period rooms. The grounds feature beautifully landscaped gardens, including a Victorian Walled Garden that the Garden Restaurant overlooks. Visitors can relax there with homemade treats and enjoy views of Torc and Mangerton mountains.

Muckross Traditional Farms recreates 1930s rural Ireland, using traditional horsepower and machinery. Here, families can meet friendly farm animals, visit a blacksmith’s forge, carpenter’s workshop, and schoolhouse, and enjoy a woodland playground and petting farm. A free shuttle bus is available for those with little legs.

Opening times vary by season. Muckross House and Gardens are open daily all year round except the Christmas period. Muckross Traditional Farms is open from mid-March to February with varying schedules, but closes fully from November to February. No pre-booking is required; tickets can be purchased on arrival. Parking is free for cars and coaches. Most areas are wheelchair accessible, though some historic sections have limited access. A courtesy transit wheelchair is available for use inside Muckross House only. The Craft Centre offers hand-thrown pottery and local textiles.
